english.standardoffencewording:

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) IMPORTANT NOTE: In relation to any offence of making/selling counterfeit tapes/compact disc's/records of music, films or games, or the infringing of trade marks, the police service may obtain FREE expert advice and assistance in their investigations from the British Phonographic Industry Anti-Piracy Unit.
Furthermore the Anti Piracy Unit will arrange FREE OF CHARGE the forensic examination of computers etc, the preparation of the appropriate statements of evidence and the attendance of expert witnesses at court. For more information see British Phonographic Industry. Officers of the Anti Piracy Unit may be contacted at ANY time.
In any enquiry relating to the manufacture or distribution of pirate films, including via the Internet, you can contact FACT (Federation Against Copyright Theft) who can provide you with assistance and advice. FACT has local investigators covering the whole of the UK and operates within the spirit of RIPA, Data Protection Act and Human Rights Act. FACT services include forensic examination of discs and computers, analysis of data using i2 software and NIM and the provision of training and intelligence on matters relating to film piracy.
(ii) See also offence wordings H2420, H2429 and H2431.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
